title: Adding a cafe, sip-and-blow events or public gatherings to a glass studio: Health District food permit, food and beverage tax, Virginia ABC license, temporary events
question: My Albemarle County glass studio wants a small cafe or bar and to host sip-and-blow classes, openings and other events. What do I need from the Blue Ridge Health District, the County (food and beverage tax, fire permits) and Virginia ABC, and what does a one-off event need?
office: Blue Ridge Health District, Office of Environmental Health, Charlottesville/Albemarle Health Department (food establishment plan review and permits); Department of Finance & Budget, Office of Revenue Administration (food and beverage tax, ABC flat fee); Virginia Alcoholic Beverage Control Authority (ABC licenses); Albemarle County Fire Rescue, Community Risk & Resilience (assembly, open flame and tent permits); Albemarle County Service Authority (grease control)
summary: A cafe inside the studio is a restaurant under Virginia law and needs a Virginia Department of Health permit to operate a food establishment, issued by the Blue Ridge Health District's Charlottesville/Albemarle office. The process starts before construction: submit the Plan Review Application and the Application for Foodservice Establishment Permit at least 30 days before opening or starting renovation (the district's new-facility page states an $80 application fee; its 2019 fee schedule lists $40 plan review and a $40 annual permit), reply to the plan review letter, finish the build-out, get the certificate of occupancy, and pass a pre-opening inspection booked at least three days ahead with a certified food manager on hand. The permit is annual, posted and not transferable. The County then collects a 6% food and beverage tax on everything you serve, remitted monthly by the 20th, and the Health District inspects at least once a year. Alcohol at sip-and-blow events needs a Virginia ABC license: a retail on-and-off-premises wine and beer license ($195 application fee plus $450 a year) or a mixed beverage restaurant license ($1,050 a year up to 100 seats) for regular service, or a $40 per-event banquet license, plus the County's ABC flat fee (beer and wine on premises $37.50 a year). Food served at a one-off event needs a temporary food establishment permit ($40) unless the cafe's own permit covers it; gatherings over 50 people need the Fire Marshal's place of assembly permit; candles in a dining area need the open flames permit; an event tent over 900 square feet needs a tent permit. If you are on public sewer, the Albemarle County Service Authority requires a grease (FOG) collection device and FOG permit for food service.

legal_basis.quote: 1. Any place where food is prepared for service to the public on or off the premises, or any place where food is served, including lunchrooms, short order places, cafeterias, coffee shops, cafes, taverns, delicatessens, dining accommodations of public or private clubs, kitchen facilities of hospitals and nursing homes, dining accommodations of public and private schools and institutions of higher education, and kitchen areas of local correctional facilities subject to standards adopted under § 53.1-68 .

No person shall own, establish, conduct, maintain, manage, or operate any hotel, restaurant, summer camp, or campground in this Commonwealth unless the hotel, restaurant, summer camp, or campground is licensed as provided in this chapter.

The Commissioner shall cause each restaurant, summer camp, and campground in the Commonwealth to be inspected at least annually, with no more than 12 months elapsing between each such inspection, in accordance with applicable provisions of this title and the regulations of the Board.

If at any time the Commissioner finds that a hotel, restaurant, summer camp, or campground is not in compliance with applicable provisions of this title or regulations of the Board, he may revoke or suspend the license of that hotel, restaurant, summer camp, or campground.
Permits shall not be issued to newly constructed or extensively remodeled food establishments until a certificate of occupancy has been issued by the Building Official.
Permits issued shall not be transferable from one person to another or from one location to another.
The permit shall be posted in every food establishment in a place where it is readily observable by the public transacting business with the establishment.
Permits shall expire annually otherwise not to exceed 12 months from the date of issuance.
"Temporary food establishment" means a food establishment that operates for a period of no more than 14 consecutive days in conjunction with a single event or celebration.

Any county is hereby authorized to levy a tax on food and beverages sold, for human consumption, by a restaurant, as such term is defined in § 35.1-1 , not to exceed six percent of the amount charged for such food and beverages.
The term "beverage" as set forth herein means alcoholic beverages as defined in § 4.1-100 and nonalcoholic beverages served as part of a meal.

Hotels, restaurants, and clubs, which shall authorize the licensee to sell wine and beer (i) in closed containers for off-premises consumption or (ii) for on-premises consumption, either with or without meals, in dining areas and other designated areas of such restaurants, or in dining areas, private guest rooms, and other designated areas of such hotels or clubs, for consumption only in such rooms and areas.
Such license may be granted only to persons who operate a restaurant that complies with the food-to-beverage ratio provisions set by Board regulation pursuant to § 4.1-111 .

Banquet licenses to persons in charge of private banquets, and to duly organized nonprofit corporations or associations in charge of special events, which shall authorize the licensee to sell or give wine and beer in rooms or areas approved by the Board for the occasion for on-premises consumption in such rooms or areas.

Every person intending to apply for any license authorized by this chapter shall file with the Board an application on forms provided by the Board and a statement in writing by the applicant swearing and affirming that all of the information contained therein is true.
Each license application fee, including annual banquet and annual mixed beverage banquet, shall be $195
For each on-and-off premises wine and beer license, $450.
(1) With a seating capacity at tables for up to 100 persons, $1,050;
(1) Banquet license, $40 per license granted by the Board, except for banquet licenses granted by the Board pursuant to subsection A of § 4.1-215 , which shall be $100 per license;
Open flames and candles. An operational permit is required to use open flames or candles in connection with assembly areas or dining areas of restaurants or drinking establishments.

legal_basis.paraphrase: A business that prepares and serves food or drink collects the County's food and beverage tax and remits it by the 20th of the next month.

legal_basis.quote: An operational permit is required to operate a place of assembly (greater than 50 persons).

legal_basis.citation: Blue Ridge Health District, Applying for New Foodservice Facility Permit page (live, last updated by the district June 2026)
Albemarle County Service Authority, Compliance Programs page (Internet Archive copy of 6 March 2026)
legal_basis.quote: Food service and other establishments are required to have a Fats, Oils and Grease (FOG) collection system.

steps.step: Decide the food model: in-house cafe, caterer or commissary, or no food at all
steps.who: You; the Charlottesville/Albemarle Health Department food team
steps.how: Any place where food is prepared for or served to the public is a restaurant under Virginia law and needs a Health Department permit; so does a coffee bar with pastries or a bar serving snacks. If you only host events catered by a permitted caterer, the caterer's permit covers the food and your studio needs no food permit (but still the fire and ABC pieces below). If your cafe will also cater off site, or share a kitchen with another operator, the Health District's commissary and incubator kitchen guidance applies and each operator needs its own permit. Prepackaged, shelf-stable goods made elsewhere are outside this process. Call or email the Charlottesville/Albemarle Environmental Health office early; the district recommends a pre-application consultation for shared kitchens.
steps.basis: Va. Code §§ 35.1-1, 35.1-18; Blue Ridge Health District, Applying for New Foodservice Facility Permit page (live)
steps.quote: If a food facility plans to cater from a shared, commissary kitchen, both the commissary kitchen and the caterer will need to apply for separate permits.

steps.step: Submit the Health District plan review and permit applications before construction and at least 30 days before opening
steps.who: You (the owner of record); Blue Ridge Health District, Environmental Health, Charlottesville/Albemarle office
steps.how: Whenever a food establishment is built, remodeled or converted from another use, plans and specifications go to the Health Department before the work starts, and construction cannot begin until the commercial plan review is complete. Submit the Plan Review Application and the Application for Foodservice Establishment Permit to the Environmental Health office at 1138 Rose Hill Drive (the district's page states an $80 application fee; its July 2019 fee schedule lists $40 for plan review and $40 for the annual permit). Include scaled drawings (for example 1/4 inch to the foot) showing the equipment layout with makes and models, an overall site plan with dumpsters, grease and waste oil containers, and any well or septic, the proposed menu including catered and seasonal items, and the projected meals per day. The owner must apply at least 30 days before opening or starting renovation. The district page also tells you to start the building permit with the local Building Official and the business license with the County at the same time.
steps.deadline: Before construction, remodeling or conversion begins; at least 30 days before opening or starting renovation
steps.fee: $80 application fee per the district's new-facility page (its 2019 fee schedule shows $40 plan review plus $40 annual permit)
steps.basis: 12VAC5-421-3610; Blue Ridge Health District, Applying for New Foodservice Facility Permit page (live); District Environmental Health Fee Schedule effective July 1, 2019
steps.quote: Note: Construction of the food establishment cannot begin until the Health Department has completed its commercial plan review process.

steps.step: Answer the plan review approval letter in writing
steps.who: You; the Environmental Health Specialist who reviewed the plans
steps.how: After review the district sends a letter listing changes needed and noting the application is approved for construction. Reply in writing to the specialist saying how you will comply, and send corrected drawings or specifications where asked. Build to the approved plans (finishes, hand sinks, three-compartment and prep sinks, refrigeration, ventilation and grease control).
steps.deadline: Before construction proceeds on the changed items
steps.basis: Blue Ridge Health District, Applying for New Foodservice Facility Permit page (live)
steps.quote: STEP 3: Send a written reply to the EHS who sent you the above letter State how you will comply with any changes noted or submit the requested specifications or other documentation.

steps.step: Get the building permit work done and the certificate of occupancy issued
steps.who: Your contractors; Community Development Building Inspections
steps.how: The cafe build-out is part of the commercial building and trade permits (glass_studio_building_mechanical): range hoods ($30 mechanical line) and hood suppression systems ($35), plumbing fixtures ($10 each), and electrical. The Health Department will not issue the food permit for a newly built or extensively remodeled space until the Building Official has issued the certificate of occupancy, so schedule the final inspections before the pre-opening inspection.
steps.deadline: Certificate of occupancy before the Health permit
steps.quote: Permits shall not be issued to newly constructed or extensively remodeled food establishments until a certificate of occupancy has been issued by the Building Official.

steps.step: Book and pass the pre-opening inspection
steps.who: You and your person in charge; Environmental Health Specialist
steps.how: When construction is complete and the equipment is in place, contact the specialist who sent the approval letter to schedule the pre-opening inspection, calling at least three days ahead. Have the certificate of occupancy document available; have at least one employee with supervisory authority present who holds a current Food Safety Manager Certification; set refrigerators to hold food at 41 degrees F or lower and freezers at 0 degrees F or lower with working thermometers; and have the facility clean with no construction material in the kitchen. The permit is then issued in the owner's name; post it where customers can see it. It is annual (not more than 12 months), not transferable to a new owner or location, and the district inspects at least once a year; later expansion or changes must be reported to the local health department.
steps.deadline: Request the inspection at least 3 days ahead; permit annual
steps.fee: $40 annual food service permit (district fee schedule)
steps.basis: 12VAC5-421-3660(B), (C), (D), (E); Va. Code § 35.1-22; Blue Ridge Health District, Applying for New Foodservice Facility Permit page (live)
steps.quote: Please call at least 3 days before the day you would like the inspection to take place.

steps.step: Register for and remit the County's 6% food and beverage tax
steps.who: You; Office of Revenue Administration, Business & Personal Tax Unit
steps.how: Register with the Business & Personal Tax Unit when you get the business license (glass_studio_business_license). Collect 6% on all food and beverages sold, including alcoholic beverages and nonalcoholic beverages served with a meal, and file and pay online at albemarlecountytaxes.org or on the printable form by the 20th of each month for the previous month. The County's list of taxed establishments includes cafes, coffee shops, caterers and taverns. Sales tax (5.3%) is separately registered with the Virginia Department of Taxation.
steps.fee: 6 percent of what is charged for the food and drink sold
steps.basis: Va. Code § 58.1-3833; Albemarle County Finance & Budget, Food & Beverage Tax page (Internet Archive copy of 14 August 2026)
steps.paraphrase: The tax is 6% of what customers are charged for food and drink.

steps.step: For alcohol: pick the Virginia ABC license that fits, apply, post the notice, and pay the state and County fees
steps.who: You; Virginia Alcoholic Beverage Control Authority; Office of Revenue Administration
steps.how: For regular sip-and-blow sessions or a studio bar, the usual retail licenses are the on-and-off-premises wine and beer license for a restaurant (application fee $195 plus a $450 annual state license tax) and, for spirits, the mixed beverage restaurant license ($1,050 a year up to 100 seats), which requires a restaurant meeting ABC's food-to-beverage ratio; both presuppose the Health Department permit. For occasional private events a banquet license ($40 per license) is issued per event, processed in about 7 to 10 days on ABC's page, against about 60 days for retail licenses. File the ABC application with the sworn statement, post the notice of application on the front door for at least 10 and not more than 30 days (retail licenses), and pay the application fee plus any fingerprint processing cost. Then pay the County's ABC flat fee each year (beer and wine on premises $37.50; mixed beverages up to 100 seats $200). ABC's licensing portal was not opened and its pages refuse automated readers; confirm current fees on abc.virginia.gov.
steps.deadline: Retail licenses: about 60 days processing (ABC page, 2023); banquet licenses: 7 to 10 days; notice posted 10 to 30 days
steps.fee: ABC application $195 per license plus fingerprint costs; annual state tax $450 (wine and beer on-and-off premises), $1,050 (mixed beverage restaurant, up to 100 seats), $40 per banquet license; County flat fee $37.50 (beer and wine on premises) or $200 (mixed beverages, up to 100 seats)
steps.basis: Va. Code §§ 4.1-206.3, 4.1-230, 4.1-231.1; Albemarle County Finance & Budget, Tax Rates page (Internet Archive copy of 17 April 2026); Virginia ABC, Get a License page (Internet Archive copy of 30 November 2023)
steps.quote: Approximate processing time: Banquet Licenses: 7-10 days Retail and Industry Licenses/Permits: 60 days

steps.step: For a one-off event with food: temporary food establishment permit and event coordinator application
steps.who: You or your food vendor; Blue Ridge Health District Environmental Health
steps.how: A temporary food establishment operates for no more than 14 consecutive days at a single event. A vendor cooking or sampling food at your event who does not hold a current VDH permit for that operation submits the district's Temporary Food Establishment Permit Application to the Charlottesville/Albemarle office ($40 temporary event fee; no fee for churches, schools, 501(c)(3)s and volunteer fire and rescue organizations, who still file). If your studio is the event host with several vendors, the Event Coordinator submits the Temporary Event Coordinator Application with the vendor list, a layout map showing toilets and waste disposal, and the water supply (a private well must be tested at least annually for nitrates and total coliforms). The permit is posted and valid only for the stated period.
steps.deadline: Before the event (apply early; no district lead time was stated on the page)
steps.fee: $40 temporary event fee for vendors (district fee schedule); no fee for the listed nonprofit organizations
steps.basis: 12VAC5-421-10; Blue Ridge Health District, Temporary Events page (live); District Environmental Health Fee Schedule effective July 1, 2019
steps.quote: If you are planning on operating as a food vendor at a temporary event in the Blue Ridge Health District (including Charlottesville City, Counties of Albemarle, Louisa, Greene, Fluvanna and Nelson) you will be required to obtain a Temporary Food Establishment Permit.

steps.step: Fire Marshal permits for gatherings, candles and tents
steps.who: You; Albemarle County Fire Rescue, Community Risk & Resilience
steps.how: Classes, openings and events that bring more than 50 people into the studio need the Fire Marshal's place of assembly permit ($200 a year per location) and an occupant load the building permit allows. Candles or open flames in a dining or drinking area need the open flames and candles permit ($200 a year, or $100 if ancillary to another permit) and must follow the Fire Marshal's open-flame decorative device guidelines. An outdoor event tent over 900 square feet or 50 occupants needs a tent permit ($100 to $300 depending on lead time, valid 30 days). Food trucks at your event must show a current fire inspection from their home jurisdiction. Details are in glass_studio_fire_permits.
steps.deadline: Before the first event; tent permit cheapest when applied for 30 days ahead
steps.fee: Places of assembly $200 per year; open flames and candles $200 or $100; tents $100 to $300
steps.basis: 13VAC5-52-70 (SFPC Table 107.2); Albemarle County Fire Rescue, Permits & Inspections page (Internet Archive copy of 14 August 2026)
steps.quote: An operational permit is required to use open flames or candles in connection with assembly areas, dining areas of restaurants or drinking establishments.
steps.paraphrase: Using candles or open flames in assembly or dining areas needs an operational permit.

steps.step: If you are on public sewer: install a grease collection device and get the ACSA FOG permit
steps.how: The Albemarle County Service Authority requires food service establishments to have a Fats, Oils and Grease collection system (grease interceptor or trap), installed, inspected and maintained under its FOG Program; it publishes a New Restaurant Packet, FOG Permit Application Instructions and a FOG Permit Application. Size and locate the device on the plumbing plans so the Health District plan review, the building permit and ACSA all see the same thing. Outside the ACSA service area, grease goes to your septic system and the Health District's onsite sewage rules apply.
steps.fee: Not stated on the pages read (ask ACSA)
steps.basis: Albemarle County Service Authority, Compliance Programs page (Internet Archive copy of 6 March 2026)
steps.quote: Food service and other establishments are required to have a Fats, Oils and Grease (FOG) collection system.

escalation.trigger: The Health District refuses, suspends or revokes the food permit, or you dispute an inspection finding
escalation.next: Discuss with the district's Environmental Health manager; a licensing decision under Title 35.1 is an agency case decision reviewable under the Virginia Administrative Process Act (informal fact-finding, then circuit court)
escalation.deadline: Per the Administrative Process Act and the notice you receive; no district deadline was published on the pages read
escalation.basis: Va. Code § 35.1-22; Va. Code § 2.2-4000 et seq. (not read here)
escalation.quote: If at any time the Commissioner finds that a hotel, restaurant, summer camp, or campground is not in compliance with applicable provisions of this title or regulations of the Board, he may revoke or suspend the license of that hotel, restaurant, summer camp, or campground.

escalation.trigger: The Fire Marshal refuses or conditions an assembly, open flame or tent permit
escalation.next: Local Board of Fire Prevention Code Appeals, then the State Building Code Technical Review Board (see glass_studio_fire_permits)
escalation.deadline: 14 calendar days (local board); 21 calendar days (State Review Board)
escalation.quote: The appeal shall be submitted to the LBFPCA within 14 calendar days of the application of the SFPC.

caveats: The Blue Ridge Health District pages were read live on 2026-10-19; the district's fee schedule PDF is dated July 1, 2019 and lists $40 plan review and $40 annual permit, while the district's new-facility page (last updated June 2026) states an $80 application fee for the two applications together. Confirm the current amount with the Rose Hill Drive office.

abc.virginia.gov refuses automated readers and its newest Internet Archive copies are from 2023; the ABC processing times come from that copy, and the license types and fees come from the Code of Virginia (§§ 4.1-206.3, 4.1-230, 4.1-231.1, read live). ABC regulations on the food-to-beverage ratio and on 'sip and paint'-style event venues were not read; ask ABC which license fits a studio that is not a full restaurant.
The County's Food & Beverage Tax page and Tax Rates page are Internet Archive copies (dates in the sources) and the County's quotes carry paraphrases because its terms bar reposting.
serviceauthority.org refuses automated readers; the ACSA FOG statement is from the Internet Archive copy of its Compliance Programs page (6 March 2026). FOG permit fees were not found.
The Health District's Plan Review Application, permit application, temporary event application and the ACSA FOG documents were not opened; their contents and fillability are not described.

Whether the studio's demonstration or class space is an Assembly occupancy under the building code is a Building Official decision; the Fire Marshal's place of assembly permit applies at more than 50 persons.
